mobile and immobile managerial career paths are different in several respects, but are also similar in other ways.
mobile and immobile managerial careers differ in terms of timing and context.
mobile managers are younger, more likely to be men, more likely to have a higher level position, more likely to work in larger organizations and are more likely to be in a professional occupation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the timing, direction, and type of mobility events in the careers of mobile and immobile middle managers and the contextual factors associated with these events.
the timing of managerial career events, and with the role of contextual factors in shaping career paths.
the timing of mobility events, the movement direction of mobility events and the type of mobility event.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mobile and immobile managerial careers are different in timing, direction, and context.
mobile managers have a different career path from immobile managers, and the differences are not just in terms of the number of moves.
mobile managers are more likely to have more frequent mobility, more frequent changes in position, and more frequent changes in employer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mobile managers tend to have more frequent mobility events and are more likely to have upward movement in their careers.
the career patterns of managers can be differentiated by mobility and that contextual factors influence these patterns.
mobile managers have a more varied career path and are more likely to move into new positions, while immobile managers have a less diverse career path and are less likely to move into a new position.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mobile and immobile careers are distinct and that contextual factors influence the nature and direction of career movement.
the career paths of managers are highly dependent on their context and that the career paths are not necessarily the result of individual career choices.
career paths are shaped by both individual and organizational factors.
